result.title: Point Dynamics as Proxy for Robotic World Models
result.summary: Robotic world models predict future video frames from the current observation and a sequence of robot actions. While recent models follow the given actions closely, manipulated objects often collapse or move inconsistently with the action. We attribute this to the conditioning: an action, or a rendering of the robot, specifies where the robot goes but not how the scene responds, leaving a single video model to infer the interaction dynamics implicitly while also rendering appearance. We therefore separate dynamics prediction from visual rendering, with 3D point dynamics as the proxy between them. Specifically, we lift the first frame into 3D points, simulate how they respond to the robot's motion with a learned point dynamics model, and render the simulated points back into pixel-aligned videos that any video model can read. In controlled experiments on the DROID dataset with two video renderers of different architectures, this point dynamics proxy reduces object motion error by 8.6% and 6.2% without degrading image quality, and by 8.1% on a real bimanual robot. Moreover, the video follows the simulation: more accurate dynamics yield more accurate object motion, and editing the points steers the video. This suggests that advances in dynamics modeling can translate into more faithful robotic world models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把3D点动态作为机器人世界模型中的间代理：将首帧提升为点云，用学习到的点动态模型模拟点对机器人动作的响应，再渲染成像素对齐视频供视频模型读取，从而把动态预测与视觉渲染解耦。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「显式中间状态承载动态、生成模型只负责外观」的分工，可能为 LVR 中把任务必要的变化信息放入可检查的中间表示、避免交给生成模型隐式推断提供线索；但点状态是否承载语义与证据筛选、能否迁移到 VLM 推理仍需核查。
